questions.q: What three requirements does Finance's request point to, before any AWS service is named?
options: Logic that runs the same way every time, a destination built for repeated joins, and types fixed once centrally
A bigger S3 bucket, a faster internet connection, and a new IAM user
A requirement to delete the raw data once it's processed
A requirement to query only through the AWS console, never from code
questions.explain: Those three requirements — repeatable logic, a warehouse-grade destination, and centralized type-fixing — are what point to an ETL job plus a warehouse, not any specific service name.

questions.q: Where does the Glue ETL job write its output?
options: A curated S3 zone, as Parquet, before any separate load step brings it into Redshift
Directly into Redshift tables, with no intermediate storage
Back into the same raw S3 zone, overwriting the original files
Into a local file on the Glue worker, deleted after each run
questions.explain: The job writes cleaned, typed, deduplicated Parquet to the curated S3 zone; a separate COPY step (Lesson 5) loads that into Redshift.

questions.q: Why does a curated S3 zone matter for Lesson 7's Athena queries?
options: Because the curated Parquet exists independently in S3, Lesson 7 can query it there through Redshift Spectrum without touching the warehouse
Because Athena cannot read from Redshift under any circumstance
Because S3 storage is required for any Glue job to run at all
It has no connection to Lesson 7 at all
questions.explain: Because the curated data is durable Parquet in S3, Lesson 7 can query it directly via Redshift Spectrum for occasional joins, independent of the warehouse.

questions.q: Why is Redshift Serverless chosen over an always-on provisioned cluster?
options: Northfield's query pattern is bursty around month-end, and Serverless auto-pauses and bills per RPU-second
Provisioned clusters cannot run SQL joins
Serverless is required for any table to have a DISTKEY or SORTKEY
An always-on cluster would be cheaper for this exact workload
questions.explain: Serverless's auto-pause and per-RPU-second billing fits a bursty, month-end-heavy query pattern far better than paying for always-on capacity sized for the busiest day.

questions.q: What is the previewed shape of the Redshift warehouse this chapter builds?
options: A small star schema: one fact table at order-line grain, plus three dimension tables
A single flat table with every column from the raw CSV
Twelve separate fact tables, one per region
No tables at all — Redshift is used only as a staging area
questions.explain: Lesson 4 builds exactly one fact table (fact_orders) and three dimension tables (dim_product, dim_customer, dim_date) under the analytics schema — nothing more than Finance and Ops actually need.
